ObsPy is a Python framework for processing seismological data. It provides parsers for common file formats, clients to access data centers, and seismological signal processing routines that allow the manipulation of seismological time series. The goal of the ObsPy project is to facilitate rapid application development for seismology.

This overview document provides a high-level understanding of ObsPy's architecture, core components, and functionality. For more detailed information about specific components, please refer to the corresponding documentation sections.

Core Architecture
-----------------

ObsPy follows a modular architecture centered around fundamental data structures that represent seismological data. The system is designed to provide a consistent API across different data formats and processing functions.

Sources: [README.md 22-24](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/README.md#L22-L24)[obspy/core/trace.py 3-10](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/trace.py#L3-L10)

Core Data Structures
--------------------

### Stream and Trace

The fundamental data structures in ObsPy are the `Stream` and `Trace` classes. A `Stream` object is a container for multiple `Trace` objects, which represent individual time series data.

Each `Trace` has a NumPy array containing the time series data and a `Stats` object that holds metadata like network, station, channel codes, and timing information.

Sources: [obspy/core/stream.py 305-339](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/stream.py#L305-L339)[obspy/core/trace.py 289-327](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/trace.py#L289-L327)[obspy/core/trace.py 29-143](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/trace.py#L29-L143)

### UTCDateTime

The `UTCDateTime` class provides precise time handling essential for seismological data. It extends Python's datetime functionality with features needed for geophysical time series data.

### Event and Catalog

The `Event` class represents a seismic event with associated metadata (origin, magnitude, focal mechanism). A `Catalog` is a collection of `Event` objects.

### Inventory

The `Inventory` class contains station metadata including networks, stations, and channels.

Sources: [obspy/core/stream.py 41-91](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/stream.py#L41-L91)[obspy/core/trace.py 1-14](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/trace.py#L1-L14)

I/O System
----------

ObsPy can read and write a wide variety of seismological file formats through its plugin-based I/O system. The system is designed to provide a consistent API regardless of the underlying format.

The main entry points for reading data are:

*   `read()` - for waveform data
*   `read_inventory()` - for station metadata
*   `read_events()` - for event data

Each supported format registers handlers for these functions, allowing for automatic format detection and consistent API across formats.

Sources: [obspy/core/util/base.py 52-63](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/core/util/base.py#L52-L63)[setup.py 153-501](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/setup.py#L153-L501)

Signal Processing
-----------------

ObsPy provides a comprehensive set of signal processing functions for seismological data analysis:

These processing functions can be applied directly to `Stream` and `Trace` objects with a consistent interface. Most operations modify the data in-place and add an entry to the processing history.

Sources: [obspy/signal/interpolation.py 1-9](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/obspy/signal/interpolation.py#L1-L9)[setup.py 502-570](https://github.com/obspy/obspy/blob/d650ebd3/setup.py#L502-L570)

Client Interfaces

Plugin System
-------------

ObsPy uses an entry point system to register plugins for various functionalities:

1.   **Waveform formats**: Plugins for reading and writing time series data
2.   **Event formats**: Plugins for reading and writing seismic event data
3.   **Inventory formats**: Plugins for reading and writing station metadata
4.   **Processing operations**: Plugins for detrending, filtering, interpolation, etc.

This architecture makes it easy to extend ObsPy with new formats and algorithms.

Summary
-------

ObsPy provides a comprehensive Python framework for seismological data processing with:

*   Core data structures for time series, station metadata, and event data
*   Support for reading and writing numerous file formats
*   Extensive signal processing capabilities
*   Client interfaces for accessing remote data
*   Visualization tools for seismological data

The modular design makes it flexible for various applications, from quick data inspection to complex batch processing pipelines.
